title: Binary Berlekamp simultaneous-coset square-root bound
statement: For every integer ell >= 2, n equal to 2 ell + 1 or 2 ell + 2, and 1 <= d < ell, put k=n-d. In every simultaneous coset of monic constant-one degree-k binary polynomials obtained by fixing coefficients above degree d and inverse coefficients above degree d modulo x^(ell+1), the square of the polynomial-Mobius sum is at most 2d times the squarefree population of the coset.

provenance.source: Axeyum gf2-lemire lane; exact shift-correlation decomposition of the Berlekamp-inverse annihilator energy

notes: The bounded operation binary_berlekamp_annihilator_energy_report checks this inequality in both endpoint windows through ell=9 and reports the worst fibre ratio, but finite enumeration is not evidence for the universal statement. Selected release probes also preserve it at every tail order ceil(2ell/3)<=d<ell for both endpoints at ell=10,11,12; those twenty rows remain uncredited diagnostics. The support is no longer unclassified: binary_artin_schreier_kernel_report proves the exact kernel dimension after reducing every inverse-shift collision to f^2+h f=a in a truncated binary local ring, and every shift row checks the resulting unsigned ceiling. What remains conjectural is cancellation of the Mobius-Berlekamp signs on those affine fibres. A proposed single-translation involution proof is ruled out by the finite row (ell,k,d)=(9,11,8): the best translation defect has square 54^2>2d*88 even though the actual signed inequality holds. The operation binary_second_trace_arf_report independently identifies every squarefree sign through factorization, the integral discriminant modulo eight, and the second-trace Arf invariant through degree ten. Its per-polynomial nondegenerate rank evaluates the same sign but does not by itself prove joint fibre cancellation. Summing the conjectured local inequality and using the proved exact diagonal Q_k=(2^k-(-1)^k)/3 yields E<=2d Q_k<d 2^k and strict weighted-term bounds from d=210 for both ell=300 endpoints. This remains only a tail input and does not control the complementary low block or prove Lemire's theorem.
